game_moneyline_spread#cfbd_fcs_coverage.rationale: The fallback the gap asks for already exists: cfb.lower_division_game_margin_model (ridge score-based margin rating per division, margin cap 35, home edge, posterior SD) is attached to game_moneyline_spread, and HIGHSCORE uses cfb.season_max_total_tail, not FCS ratings. What remains is which CFBD endpoints cover FCS plays, drives and SP+ by season, a source-coverage check.

game_moneyline_spread#pace_attachment.rationale: cfb.pace, cfb.drives and cfb.offense_style are all defined and attached to s4; the open question is their relative weight and redundancy for margin variance, which the stated heteroskedasticity test on historical possession counts settles. No input is missing.

game_stat_props#receiving_yards_definiti.rationale: Settlement follows official NCAA statistics; the sampled rule already excludes 2-point yards and counts OT. Laterals and negative yards affect only the settled figure, not which inputs (completion_yardage_profile, player_usage, script) are needed. Full Kalshi rules text plus a reconciliation sample close it; no catalog input changes.

game_stat_props#situational_effect_untes.rationale: The catalog already defines cfb.rest_travel (days rest, bye, travel distance/time zone, kickoff time, rivalry and next-opponent importance flags) and cfb.motivation; whether they move passing volume at the 20-30 yard threshold scale is an effect-size question the proposed residual regression settles, attachment following the result.

game_total#explosive_dispersion.rationale: cfb.success_explosiveness already defines opponent-adjusted IsoPPP and an explosive-dependence index, and cfb.nonoffensive_scoring_rate covers non-offensive TDs; choosing IsoPPP versus 20+ yard rate for tail calibration is a held-out backtest comparison, not missing catalog content.

game_total#situational_totals_effect.rationale: Rest, lookahead and rivalry flags are defined in cfb.rest_travel and title/eligibility stakes in cfb.motivation; their effect on tempo and totals is unestablished, which is exactly the residual regression on non-market expected totals described. Attachment is a consequence of that test, not a missing definition.

overtime#late_decision_causality.rationale: cfb.end_regulation_decision_profile operationally defines the situations (Q4 clock <=2:00, trailing by 1-3 or 8, tied) and the aggressive-vs-kneel choice from play-by-play with a logistic fit; validating the automated label against 200 hand-labelled states is a measurement-accuracy check.

overtime#ot_rule_history.rationale: Verified (NCAA.org 2021, NCAA.com): 2-point try mandatory from 3rd OT through 2018; 2019-2020 alternating 2-point plays from 5th OT; from 2021, 2-point try required in 2nd OT and alternating 2-point plays from 3rd OT. cfb.ot_model, cfb.two_point_shootout_rate and cfb.clock_rules regime indicators already carry this; the input list is unchanged, only historical frequency effects remain.

quarter_and_half_sides#period_matchup_ga.rationale: Period structure is already represented by cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential, cfb.first_drive, cfb.opening_poss and cfb.two_minute_drill_efficiency; whether team-level period-share residuals persist beyond noise is the stated cross-season correlation test, a data question.

quarter_and_half_totals#garbage_threshol.rationale: Verified: the published S&P+/SP+ update (Football Study Hall, 2019) uses margins above 43 (Q1), 37 (Q2), 27 (Q3) and 21 (Q4), matching cfb.garbage_time_scoring_profile's Q3>27 and Q4>21. The input definition stands; only the +/-7 sensitivity and any FCS variant remain, both data checks.

quarter_and_half_totals#opponent_matchup.rationale: Season-level opponent-adjusted cfb.off_ppa/def_ppa plus cfb.period_share_of_total and cfb.team_period_points_share already define the period-total inputs; whether period-specific efficiencies add out-of-sample log-loss value is a model-comparison test.

quarter_and_half_totals#quarter_total_no.rationale: The share-of-total model (cfb.period_share_of_total, cfb.period_total_dispersion) and candidate structural inputs (first_drive, opening_poss, period_drive_clock_budget) are defined; whether structure beats the share model is the 5-season log-loss comparison, an empirical question.

season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.rationale: Checked: only one win over an FCS opponent (meeting the scholarship requirement) counts toward six, and 5-7 teams fill unfilled slots in APR order. cfb.bowl_selection_state counts raw wins >=6 and has no FCS-opponent win cap or APR source, so the definition is demonstrably wrong and needs new raw inputs (opponent division per win, APR scores).
season_futures#bowl_eligibility_rule.catalog_action: Amend cfb.bowl_selection_state: count at most one qualifying FCS win, add an opponent-division flag per game and an NCAA APR score source for the 5-7 fallback order, citing the current NCAA postseason bylaw and any 2026 waiver.

season_futures#coach_effect_gap.rationale: cfb.program_trajectory_index (attached to season_futures) already regresses rating change on a new-head-coach flag and adds coach-exit hazard in its multi-season simulation for KXNCAAFTFUT; what is open is the size of coach effect relative to talent, a fitted coefficient.

season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.rationale: cfb.cfp_committee_resume_model (season_futures) and cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features (polls_and_cfp_rankings) define the same committee rank model with different feature lists; two diverging definitions of one input is a catalog defect fixed by authoring, not data.
season_futures#committee_model_duplicati.catalog_action: Make cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features the canonical committee rank input (or the reverse), merge feature lists, and alias the other id in the season_futures and unreg:polls_and_cfp_rankings records.

season_futures#conf_count_dependence_fit.rationale: cfb.conf_schedule_win_dependence fully defines the conference shift N(0, tau_c^2) and says tau_c is to be fitted from cross-conference results; the 1.5-point start value is a calibration constant settled by fitting 2014-2025 non-conference games.

season_futures#fcs_ivy_mechanism.rationale: cfb.lower_division_title_model is no longer a sketch: it specifies a ridge score-based rating per division, 20,000-season simulation, conference tiebreaks (Ivy co-champions) and playoff bracket; validating it against past FCS/D3 playoffs is empirical. Ivy shared-title payout awaits KXNCAAFIVY rules (contract).

season_futures#playoff_format_2026.rationale: Verified (CFP release 2026-01-23, NCAA.com 2026-08-11): 2026-27 stays 12 teams, five highest-ranked conference champions get automatic bids plus seven at-large, straight seeding with top four byes, no reseeding, selection Dec 6, final Jan 25 2027; expansion not adopted. cfb.playoff_format already covers this, input list unchanged.

season_futures#seeding_rule_2026.rationale: Verified: straight seeding by final CFP ranking since 2025 (top four ranked teams get byes, conference champions keep only automatic bids), extended for 2026-27. What remains is the contract's handling of a format change before selection, which only Kalshi wording can settle.

season_futures#tfut_horizon_model.rationale: cfb.program_trajectory_index specifies the AR-type regression of rating_{t+1} on rating_t, recruiting, portal and coach terms with phi and residual SD to be fitted on 2014-2025; the 0.7/4-point values are placeholders for that fit. Post-2026 format is undecided, carried as scenarios, not a missing input.

team_total#run_defense_matchup_gap.rationale: cfb.run_defense is defined (line yards, stuff rate, rushing PPA allowed, opponent-adjusted) and attached; its incremental value over def_ppa for run-first offences and the need for rush yards allowed are the stated incremental-fit tests.

team_total#situational_effects_unmeasure.rationale: cfb.rest_travel defines rest, travel, lookahead and rivalry flags and cfb.motivation stakes; their effect on single-team scoring is unestablished, which is what the residual regression on non-market expectations decides. No definition is missing.

touchdown_scorer#kickoff_rule_regime.rationale: Verified: touchback moved to the 25 in 2012; from 2018 a fair catch inside the 25 on a kickoff is a touchback at the 25. cfb.dst_td_propensity already records kickoff rule regime by season; the effect on return-TD rates by regime is a data comparison, input list unchanged.

touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.rationale: The archetype is keyed to anytime/first player TD markets, but the ledger's live series are team and game TD counts; player-role inputs (td_rates, depth_chart, player_usage) are primary for absent series. That is a series/archetype mapping defect in the records.
touchdown_scorer#player_series_missing.catalog_action: Re-check live Kalshi CFB TD series, re-key touchdown_scorer to the live team/game TD-count series (td_count_dispersion, td_per_scoring_trip, dst_td_propensity primary) and mark the player part dormant with player inputs secondary.

touchdown_scorer#weather_effect_on_td_sp.rationale: cfb.weather_pit is defined (wind, gusts, precipitation, temperature vintages by stadium, domes ignored, effects on pass rate, totals and FG success) and attached; the size of weather effects on rush/receive TD shares and TD count is the stated multi-season test.

unreg:awards_and_honors#electorate_unsou.rationale: cfb.award_vote_feature_model is fitted separately for each award since 2010 with a ballot-date as-of cut, so electorate differences enter as per-award coefficients and do not change the input list; tabulating each body's ballot deadline sets an as-of date. Inactive AP tickers are a contract-listing matter.

unreg:awards_and_honors#finalist_procedu.rationale: The contract rule (No if no finalists announced before the winner) is clear; finalist count and announcement timing per award are historical base rates to tabulate and estimate from 2015 onward, which the existing award inputs consume. No new input or mechanism is needed.

unreg:awards_and_honors#script_effect_on.rationale: Script-dependent usage is already defined in cfb.script, cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts and cfb.script_rush_attempts; the open item is the elasticity of a candidate's carries/targets to expected margin, an estimate from historical game logs.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#dra.rationale: Verified (NFL rules/NCAA enforcement memos): eligibility requires three NFL seasons after high-school graduation; early-entry deadline mid-January (Jan 15 2025, Jan 24 for CFP finalists). This matches cfb.draft_declaration_propensity's indicator; pre/post-bowl announcement shares are data.

unreg:coaching_and_governance_events#tra.rationale: cfb.transfer_destination_candidate_model is defined (portal-entry state, destination multinomial, compensation imputed by conference tier); the missing piece is that revenue-sharing/NIL offers are not observed in any public dataset. That is an inaccessible source; re-keying would not create the data.

unreg:half_full_double_result#A-U3.rationale: cfb.clock_rules (rule-regime indicators by season with regime-specific plays and scoring) and cfb.two_point_shootout_rate are attached to this archetype; 2021 OT and 2023 clock regimes are verified dates. Whether pooled 2014+ transition matrices differ from 2023+ is a structural-break test.

unreg:half_full_double_result#A-U4.rationale: cfb.halftime_adjustment_differential is fully defined (competitive-state 2H minus 1H EPA per staff, shrunk) and flagged as a test input; split-half cross-season reliability decides keep or drop. Purely a data question.

unreg:half_full_double_result#A-U6.rationale: cfb.half_tie_conditional_win and cfb.half_to_full_transition_matrix define the tie-at-half mass and conditional winner split; the ~10 percent mass and receiver effect are magnitudes to measure on 2023+ CFBD line scores.

unreg:half_full_double_result#A-U5.rationale: Verified: Big Ten reports since 2023, SEC since 2024 (from three days out), ACC and Big 12 since 2025 (Big 12: daily from three days out, final 90 minutes pre-kickoff, five status levels); non-conference games uncovered. cfb.injuries names these; no public timestamped archive, so capture must be prospective.

unreg:multi_leg_parlay_packs#B-U2.rationale: cfb.cross_game_residual_dependence is defined and attached: pairwise correlation of backed sides from shared conference-offset posterior draws, validated on signed residuals. Whether the dependence is material for 3-4 leg packs is the stated bowl-slate back-test.

unreg:multi_leg_parlay_packs#B-U4.rationale: Conference availability-report policies cover conference games (Big Ten 2023, SEC 2024, ACC/Big 12 2025); no official report covering bowls/CFP was found. The availability input (cfb.injuries, qb_status_pit) is defined; postseason coverage is a coverage limitation of the source.

unreg:polls_and_cfp_rankings#committee_p.rationale: Checked: since 2025 the committee uses straight seeding and a reweighted strength-of-schedule plus record-strength metric; 2026-27 kept the same format. cfb.cfp_ranking_resume_features already has resume/SOR features; whether 2014-2025 weights hold after the 2025 metric change is a regime-stability fit.

unreg:season_stat_leader#C-U5.rationale: Verified policy start years: Big Ten 2023, SEC 2024, ACC and Big 12 2025, with status levels and pre-kickoff deadlines; non-conference weeks unreported. The input is defined in cfb.injuries/qb_status_pit; history with capture timestamps must be archived prospectively.

unreg:team_event_counting_specials#avail.rationale: cfb.qb_status_pit and cfb.kicker are attached and cfb.snap_weighted_availability_loss defines snap-weighted absences; the size of QB, pass-rusher or kicker changes on small sack/INT/FG counts is the stated historical effect test.

unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.rationale: cfb.opp_dropback_volume's own definition says it measures the same quantity as cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts plus cfb.state_dependent_pace and should be aliased; two definitions of one input across split archetypes is an unresolved catalog duplication.
unreg:team_event_counting_specials#stat_.catalog_action: Alias cfb.opp_dropback_volume to cfb.script_adjusted_pass_attempts (opponent view) in the team_event_counting_specials and season_stat_leader records, or document a distinct defensive-view definition.
